newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia says won't hit Iran trade.
newsitem.headline: Australia says won't hit Iran trade.

text.p: Australia said on Wednesday it would not hit trade with Iran as part of its diplomatic sanctions against the Islamic state after a German court linked Tehran to terrorism.

"Australia does not seek to interfere with the commercial negotiations, be it by the Australian Wheat Board, by a large company or by a small company, with regard to the two-way trade that exists between Australia and Iran," Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer told reporters.

Australia last week recalled its ambassador to Iran over the German court decision and is considering further action after a detailed study of the verdict and consultations with other Western governments.

The Labor opposition had demanded an immediate trade ban and the cancellation of an unused A$950 million (US736 million) line of credit to Iran. But wheat farmers argue against trade sanctions, warning they would be hard hit by a ban on their biggest market, worth A$500 million in calendar 1996.
"It is a matter that Australia does not seek to interfere with commercial activities between companies large and small ... as things stand between Australia and Iran," Fischer told reporters.
